canonical_title: Accept a bounded, deterministic, manually-triggered slice before authorizing background automation over the same capability
summary: Stage 4 of SB-ORG-LEARNING-1.1 was accepted as a bounded deterministic reconciliation wrapper -- closure/receipt matching, processed/no-op/unprocessed/reopened/conflict classification, deterministic replay, bounded local lock ownership -- with no background scheduler, no automatic trigger, and no authority effect. Stage 4B (background automation that would trigger this reconciliation and downstream candidate-learning generation without a human manually running it) was explicitly scoped out of this mission, left deferred and not authorized, and tracked as a separate GitHub issue rather than folded into this mission's acceptance.

claims.text: Stage 4 was durably accepted for its bounded, deterministic reconciliation results (processed/no-op, unprocessed, new revision, reopened/superseded, invalid/unsafe, retryable handling, deterministic replay/order, bounded local ownership/recovery, no-authority output) while Stage 4B mature background automation was explicitly recorded as not required for this mission and left deferred/not authorized.

evidence.locator: Section 'Stage 4 — ACCEPTED, bounded': lists the accepted deterministic results, then: 'Stage 4B mature automation was explicitly not required for this mission and remains deferred/not authorized.'

claims.text: The Founder/human merge authorization for the whole mission explicitly enumerates what it does not authorize, including Stage 4B, mature automation, provider/model integration, automatic promotion, governance/Product Truth mutation, production/customer mutation, and SB-P-1.12 activation -- keeping the boundary between what was proven deterministic and what remains an unproven automation surface explicit at the point of merge, not just in an earlier design document.

evidence.locator: Section 9, 'Founder merge authorization': 'This authorization is for merge of the accepted mission only. It does not authorize: Stage 4B; mature automation; provider/model integration; automatic promotion; governance/Product Truth mutation; production/customer mutation; SB-P-1.12.'

claims.text: Stage 4B was not left as an implicit gap or a note in a closing paragraph -- it was given its own canonical GitHub tracking issue (#590, 'OLE Stage 4B — Background Automation & Candidate Learning Runtime'), explicitly referenced by both post-merge governance records as the deferred capability whose purpose is to remove the manual-initiation dependency this very learning handoff had to satisfy by hand.

evidence.locator: 'Stage 4B tracking issue: #590 — OLE Stage 4B — Background Automation & Candidate Learning Runtime'; line 112: 'GitHub issue #590 tracks the deferred Stage 4B capability whose purpose is to remove this manual initiation dependency.'

conditions: Applies when a new capability could plausibly be built either as a bounded, manually-triggered, deterministic slice or as an unbounded background-automated system, and the two can be genuinely separated so the first can be proven and accepted without committing to the second.

Requires the deferred automation scope to be named and tracked as a distinct, discoverable follow-up (an issue, a numbered future stage) rather than left as an unstated assumption that the manual slice is 'basically done'.
anti_patterns: Accepting a manually-triggered proof-of-concept as if it already implied the unattended background version was safe, without a separate authorization step for the automation itself.

Letting deferred automation scope live only in a design document's aspirational section, disconnected from a trackable follow-up that later governance and learning cycles (like this one) can actually surface and act on.
